- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.5), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for 2–3 periods.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent volatility, but true outcome shows mean reversion or sharp drop, reduce forecast slope and add downward bias.
- If sentiment is flat (0.0) and model shows strong upward trend, true outcome often reverses; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- For 30-day horizon, if model is consistently above true outcome by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward correction proportional to sentiment volatility (e.g., 0.5x sentiment magnitude).
